# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 16 (Bu-Vb Pc16)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc16
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 16
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** 16. Encroaching on a monk

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Anupakhajja Sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 16) is a monastic rule in the Vinaya Piṭaka regulating dwelling etiquette among monks [SuttaCentral]. According to the rule, a monk who lies down in a dwelling belonging to the Order (*saṅgha*), encroaching upon another monk with the intention of causing him to leave, commits an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. In her study of Vinaya regulations, Ute Hüsken notes that the disciplinary ordinances requiring mutual consideration regarding shared monastic accommodations do not differ substantially between the orders of monks and nuns, grouping this rule with related dwelling regulations such as Pācittiya 17 [Hüsken 1997].

This disciplinary rule has wide parallels across Vinaya traditions [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records parallels in the Pali Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (Pc 16) and Parivāra, as well as corresponding rules in the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (Pc 112), Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha, and Bhikkhunī Parivāra [SuttaCentral]. Cross-sectarian parallels for both monks and nuns are preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan texts belonging to the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya traditions [SuttaCentral].

DharmaNexus identifies 575 Pali-internal text reuse matches across 106 canonical texts, sharing substantial formulaic phrasing with Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 17 (notably §2.2.1–2.3.1), Pārājika 2, Nissaggiya Pācittiya 26 and 19, and the *Senāsanakkhandhaka* (Kd 16) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignments, DharmaNexus detects corresponding segments in Tibetan Vinaya treatises, including the *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106-2) [DharmaNexus]. An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
